writer: Marguerite Osei-Bonsu, Operations Director, Tidewell Linen Services (commercial hospital laundry, Bristol)
request: write a linkedin post about how we cut water use a lot at our Avonmouth plant after switching to the new tunnel washer in March. we now process 14 tonnes of hospital linen a day. want to thank the night shift team, keep it humble and don't go crazy with hashtags.
hidden_facts: Water use dropped from about 11 litres per kg of linen to 6.5 litres per kg.
The tunnel washer cost £780,000 and is financed over seven years.
In the first three weeks a pH dosing fault meant a batch of 2,000 theatre gowns had to be rewashed.
Night shift lead Danny Corcoran stayed on after a 10-hour shift to recalibrate the dosing pumps with the manufacturer's engineer, who had flown in from Germany.
Marguerite thinks the laundry industry overclaims on sustainability, and Tidewell still uses gas-fired dryers.
She is not sure the savings will hold in winter, when heavier soiling usually means extra rinse cycles.
The staff have nicknamed the machine 'Big Moira'.

genre: Cold email to a potential partner
writer: Tobias Lindqvist, Co-founder, Myco Mould Packaging (mycelium-based protective packaging, Leeds)
request: draft a cold email to Priya at Hearth & Wick pitching our mycelium inserts as a replacement for their polystyrene. we can do 5,000 units a month and samples are free. ask for a quick call next week, keep it short and not salesy.
hidden_facts: Myco Mould's inserts cost about £0.62 per unit, compared with roughly £0.18 for polystyrene.
Fenwick Tea Co switched to their inserts last year, and its breakage claims fell from 3.1% to 0.9% of orders.
In July they lost 1,200 units to mould contamination after a humidity controller failed in the grow room.
Tobias saw a customer complaint about a cracked candle jar on Hearth & Wick's Instagram, which is what prompted the email.
He worries privately that the price gap will kill the deal before the breakage savings get a hearing.
Insider detail: at volumes above 10,000 units a month they can absorb part of the price difference.
The inserts take seven days to grow and break down in about 45 days in a home compost bin.

writer: Inês Carvalho, Head of Community, Lantern Hollow Games (independent tabletop game publisher, Porto)
request: need the launch email for The Tidekeepers expansion for Saltmarsh Trails. it goes live on our shop Oct 21 at €34 and adds a 5th player plus 40 new cards. people who preordered get theirs shipped first. upbeat but not cringe.
hidden_facts: The print run is 6,000 copies, and 2,300 were preordered before launch.
The expansion was delayed from June because the factory in Dongguan misprinted the tide tokens so the blue looked purple.
Playtester Ruairí Mac Giolla played more than 60 test games and suggested the lighthouse card that became the box art.
Inês thinks five-player games drag; they run about 90 minutes against roughly 60 for four players.
The Heron card was rebalanced after it won about 70% of test games.
One hidden card shows the designer's dog, Biscoito.
She is unsure whether new US import tariffs will add about €6 to shipping for American customers.

writer: Dr Hamza Qureshi, Superintendent Pharmacist, Kingsway Pharmacies (group of 8 community pharmacies, Leicester)
request: write the intro for our october newsletter. flu jabs are open at all 8 branches from 1 Oct, free for over 65s, book online or just walk in. also mention the new Oadby branch is open 8am-8pm.
hidden_facts: Last season the group gave 4,100 flu jabs across all branches, and this year the target is 5,000.
On the first Saturday last year, the walk-in queue at the Narborough Road branch reached 90 minutes.
Mrs Joan Pritchard, 91, has had her jab with them every year since 2009 and always brings the staff a packet of biscuits.
This year's vaccine stock arrived four days late from the supplier.
Hamza thinks the online booking system is clunky, and many older patients would rather phone.
Insider detail: the pharmacy receives about £10 per NHS flu jab, which barely covers staff time.
He doesn't yet know whether COVID boosters can be given at the same appointment this year, because NHS guidance is still pending.

writer: Bethany Ashworth-Kole, Head of Maintenance, Greystone Lettings (residential property management, about 1,400 homes, Manchester)
request: slack update for #maintenance: we're moving all repair tickets from the email inbox to HomeFix Hub starting Monday 2 Nov, and the old inbox goes read-only on the 16th. everyone needs to finish the training by Friday. friendly, bullet points are fine.
hidden_facts: The repairs inbox currently holds 640 unresolved emails.
Average first response time is 4.2 days, and the target with the new system is 48 hours.
A tenant at the Hulme block, Mr Okonkwo, reported a leak by email three times; the messages got lost, his ceiling collapsed, and the repair cost £3,800.
Ainsworth Plumbing, their biggest contractor, hasn't yet confirmed it will use the app.
Bethany thinks the 30-minute training video is boring and twice as long as it needs to be.
The licence costs £1.10 per home per month.
She is unsure the 16 November cutoff is realistic, because two coordinators are on leave that week.

writer: Kenji Watanabe-Hart, Rentals Desk Lead, Framewise Camera Hire (film and video equipment rental, Glasgow)
request: help me reply to a customer, Aoife Brennan, who's annoyed we kept £150 from her £600 deposit for a scratched front element on the Sigma 18-35. explain why, offer to send photos of the damage, and say we can drop it to £90 if she'd prefer. polite but firm.
hidden_facts: The repair quote from the service centre in Edinburgh is £210, so the £150 charge is already below cost.
The scratch is about 4mm long and shows clearly in the technician's photos.
The checkout inspection sheet didn't specifically log the front element's condition, which is a gap in their process.
Aoife has rented from them 11 times without a single problem.
She says the lens stayed in its case for the whole shoot.
Kenji privately suspects the damage happened on the previous rental, a music video shoot booked by a renter named Callum.
Insider detail: their insurance excess is £250, so damage like this never goes through insurance; photo-documented checkouts start next month.

writer: Gwendolyn Achterberg, Funeral Director, Achterberg & Sons Funeral Directors (family-run firm since 1952, Norwich)
request: write one paragraph for our blog on why prepaid funeral plans aren't always a good idea. mention the average funeral in Norfolk is about £4,200 and that we offer free 30 min planning chats with no obligation. honest tone, not salesy.
hidden_facts: Many plans advertised at around £3,995 leave out disbursements such as the cremation fee, which is about £1,050 locally.
When Derek Haines died, his daughter found that his £3,600 plan didn't cover the hearse to the crematorium, and she paid £480 extra.
About one in five families who come to them have a plan but can't find the paperwork.
The firm sells plans itself through a regulated provider and earns about £300 commission on each, which Gwendolyn is uneasy about.
Her honest view is that writing your wishes down and telling your family matters more than paying upfront.
She has dealt with several families left out of pocket when a plan provider collapsed.
She is unsure whether naming competitor plans on the blog would come across as petty.

writer: Siobhán Delacroix-Murphy, Founder, Nest & Desk (coworking space with on-site childcare, Cork)
request: write the 'How it works' section for our landing page, maybe 3 short steps plus an intro line, around 120 words. parents book a desk and a childcare slot in one go, sessions are 9am-1pm or 1pm-5pm, €28 per half day including the creche. we're on MacCurtain Street.
hidden_facts: The creche has 12 places and the coworking floor has 30 desks.
The creche is Tusla-registered and keeps a 1:3 staff ratio for under-twos.
Member Niamh Folan, a freelance illustrator, finished her first picture book there while her 14-month-old napped next door.
Morning sessions are oversubscribed, with about a three-week waitlist, while afternoon sessions run roughly half empty.
Insider detail: childcare costs them about €21 per slot, so €28 barely breaks even.
Siobhán hasn't decided whether to allow creche-only drop-offs without a desk booking.
She thinks most coworking sites oversell 'community', and she wants Nest & Desk to sound practical instead.

writer: Rhodri Pengelly, Operations Manager, Deepline Subsea (commercial diving contractor, Aberdeen)
request: write the intro for a job ad. we're hiring an Offshore Dive Supervisor, HSE Part I surface supplied, 28 on 28 off rotation out of Aberdeen, salary from £95k. make it sound like a decent place to work, not corporate.
hidden_facts: Deepline has 46 divers on its books.
The company has gone more than 1,100 days, about three years, without a lost-time incident.
The previous supervisor left for a rival that offered £8,000 more.
In 2024 senior supervisor Elspeth Grant called off a dive over a closing weather window; a nearby vessel had an incident that day, and the client later thanked the team.
Rhodri admits rotations sometimes stretch to 35 days when vessels are delayed.
Insider detail: they are bidding on a North Sea decommissioning contract that isn't confirmed yet.
He is unsure whether £95k will attract strong candidates in the current market.

writer: Dr Adaeze Nwankwo-Fleming, Consultant Prosthetist, Limbwise Clinic (prosthetics clinic working with the NHS, Sheffield)
request: need a short speaker bio, 3rd person, about 100 words, for the ISPO UK conference on 12 Nov. my talk is 'Fitting Children Who Keep Growing'. I'm a consultant prosthetist at Limbwise in Sheffield with 15 years experience.
hidden_facts: She has fitted around 2,000 prosthetic limbs, about 300 of them for children.
She trained in Lagos and later at the University of Strathclyde.
Her patient Theo Barraclough, aged 7, asked for a leg in Sheffield Wednesday colours and now plays junior football.
Her adjustable socket design cut refits for growing children from every 4 months to every 9 months.
The trial behind that result involved only 22 children, so she is cautious about overclaiming.
She dislikes being introduced as 'inspiring' and would rather be called practical.
Insider detail: she still hand-casts some sockets in plaster because 3D scans miss soft-tissue detail.

writer: Lukas Brandvold, Owner and Locksmith, Brandvold Lock & Key (independent locksmith, York)
request: help me write a paragraph for a personal essay about leaving my trading job in London in 2019 to become a locksmith in York. I want the moment I realised I'd made the right call. first person, reflective, not cheesy.
hidden_facts: In his last year as a bond trader he earned about £240,000; he now makes around £41,000.
The moment came at 2am one January, when he let Patience Adeyemi and her baby back into their flat in four minutes and she burst into tears.
In his first year he snapped a key inside a client's antique door and paid £600 to fix it himself.
He sometimes misses the money and feels guilty about missing it.
Insider detail: most lockouts are opened with a thin plastic shim, not by picking the lock.
He divorced in 2020 and is unsure whether to mention it in the essay.
He still wakes at 5:30am out of habit from the trading floor.

writer: Priyanka Salgado-Wren, Events Secretary, Calder Valley Astronomical Society (amateur astronomy club, Hebden Bridge)
request: write an announcement for our free public stargazing night on Saturday 14 November at Heptonstall playing field. we'll have 6 telescopes, tell people to bring warm clothes. if it's cloudy we move indoors to a talk at the Methodist hall.
hidden_facts: The last public night drew about 180 people when they expected 60, and the hot chocolate ran out within an hour.
Saturn and its rings will be the main target; Jupiter doesn't rise until late in the evening, after the event ends.
Nine-year-old Ellis Thornber saw Saturn at last year's event and has since joined as a junior member.
There is parking for only about 20 cars near the field.
Priyanka is worried that the new floodlights at the cricket club will wash out the sky.
She doesn't know yet whether the council will dim the nearby streetlights as agreed.
Insider detail: the biggest telescope is a 14-inch Dobsonian that member Harold Mistry built in his garage.
